markdown_report:
SASRec offers three starting insights: causal attention represents changing interests, but the diagnosis suggests stale evidence still influences recommendations; dot-product ranking captures associations without establishing practical compatibility; sampled BCE can separate easy pairs while leaving difficult rankings unresolved. Electronics exhibits the clearest measured weakness: 14.95% wrong pairwise rankings and a −0.4812 tenth-percentile margin. Embedding similarity near 0.5 does not justify prioritizing collapse remedies.

Related work suggests three complementary directions. TGCL4SR combines global temporal transitions with local sequence encoding, motivating cross-user evidence when individual histories are sparse. LS4SRec separates long- and short-term interests, motivating recency-dependent aggregation. gSASRec addresses sampled-BCE overconfidence, motivating an objective ablation; none establishes improvements on this benchmark.

These insights define three research directions: collaborative evidence, temporal relevance, and ranking calibration. Their common framework is:

| Component | Evidence | Intended contribution | Unresolved limitation |
|---|---|---|---|
| SASRec | Ordered personal history | Personalized sequence representation | Unsupported associations |
| Directed transitions | Training-user consecutive interactions | Evidence for plausible next steps | Association is not compatibility |
| Co-occurrence | Shared training histories | Repeated specific interests | Popularity and stale interests |
| Recency weighting | Relative interaction position | Current-interest emphasis | Position is an imperfect clock |
| Loss calibration | Sampled positive–negative scores | Difficult-case separation | Unobserved items may be relevant |

Three atomic candidates follow. Scores use O/F/U/M/D for originality, future potential, user alignment, model alignment, and implementation difficulty; higher D means harder.

| Candidate | O/F/U/M/D | Positive assessment | Negative assessment |
|---|---|---|---|
| Recent transition residual | 4/7/8/7/3 | Simple collaborative evidence targets unsupported broad matches and stale interests | Cannot establish equipment compatibility or satisfied needs |
| Learned recent/history gate | 4/7/8/6/5 | Directly adjusts temporal emphasis | Sparse histories may destabilize routing |
| Warm-start multi-negative loss | 3/7/4/8/4 | Directly targets weak separation | Does not explicitly resolve two user-facing failures |

Across candidates, originality comes from adaptation rather than a new model family; future potential depends on measurable complementarity. User alignment is strongest for temporal evidence, whereas model alignment is strongest for loss changes. Difficulty favors a sparse residual over additional trained branches.

Select **recent transition residual** at 0% progress. It explicitly targets broad unsupported recommendations through observed next-step associations and older isolated interests through recent-history weighting. Its model-facing target is Electronics’ lower-tail ranking confusion. These are hypotheses, not demonstrated improvements.

Build directed transition and normalized co-occurrence tables exclusively from training histories. Aggregate their scores over recent items with exponential decay, then blend separately normalized branch scores with SASRec. Compare each branch alone and the combined model using pinned four-category macro validation HR@10. Include zero blend weight to recover the baseline. Freeze normalization before evaluation; never normalize against the evaluator’s candidate list. Retain full-catalog simulator diagnostics separately, since sampled HR@10 does not establish full-catalog quality.

idea.description: Add a sparse, recency-weighted collaborative residual to each category’s SASRec scores. Directed transitions supply observed next-step evidence; normalized co-occurrence supplies repeated collaborative associations. Select the blend using the common macro validation HR@10.
idea.motivation: The user diagnosis identifies unsupported broad associations and excessive influence from older or isolated interactions. Recent collaborative evidence may reduce both, while improving the weak positive–negative separation measured particularly in Electronics. It cannot establish compatibility, replacement need, or satisfaction from implicit interactions alone.
idea.implementation_notes: Preserve all four datasets, routing, preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, DATA_DIR=os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'], and the SASREC_EPOCHS environment default of 200. Write checkpoints, sparse tables, normalization constants, and blend settings beneath the trial directory. Construct graph statistics only from training histories; use consecutive directed transitions and binary per-user co-occurrence with cosine normalization. Bound neighborhood storage with a fixed top-K. Fit score scales from training-only query/item samples and freeze them, ensuring identical scores under sampled-candidate and full-catalog inference. Evaluate a small prespecified blend grid, including zero, through the existing validation protocol and account for all training cost. Update the predictor writer to reproduce the complete combined score in working/predict.py. Keep DiagnosisProbe(view, device), run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), and diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis). Expose the actual combined nn.Module through view.model and preserve the compatibility methods; compute margins with the combined predictor and label embedding similarity as a SASRec-embedding diagnostic. Report metadata-category breakdowns as unavailable because categories are excluded. Do not infer review content, ratings, compatibility labels, satisfaction labels, or simulator traits.
idea.pseudocode:
for category in FOUR_CATEGORIES:
    sasrec = train_baseline(category, seed=42)
    histories = training_histories(category)
    transition = row_normalize(consecutive_transition_counts(histories))
    cooccur = cosine_normalize(binary_user_item_cooccurrence(histories))
    transition, cooccur = prune_top_k(transition, cooccur)
    scales = fit_scales_on_training_queries(sasrec, transition, cooccur)

    def score(sequence, candidate_items, weights):
        recent = last_nonpadding_items(sequence, window)
        decay = normalized_exponential_position_weights(recent)
        base = sasrec.predict(sequence, candidate_items)
        next_step = weighted_lookup(transition, recent, candidate_items, decay)
        repeated_interest = weighted_lookup(cooccur, recent, candidate_items, decay)
        return (standardize(base, scales.base)
                + weights.transition * standardize(next_step, scales.transition)
                + weights.cooccur * standardize(repeated_interest, scales.cooccur))

select_small_prespecified_grid_by_pinned_macro_validation_hr10()
save_models_tables_scales_and_settings_under_trial_directory()
write_predictor_with_identical_category_routing_and_score_function()

originality.positive: Combines recent personal history with two distinct collaborative signals in a minimal, testable residual.
originality.negative: Sequence–graph fusion and recency weighting are established techniques; novelty is limited to the task-specific formulation.

future_potential.positive: A successful residual would identify complementary evidence worth integrating into a later learned temporal gate.
future_potential.negative: Sparse transitions and popularity effects may prevent generalization, and sampled validation gains may not transfer to full-catalog recommendations.

code_difficulty.positive: Sparse counting and lookup avoid an additional neural training stage and preserve the baseline encoder.
code_difficulty.negative: Training-only normalization, efficient full-catalog scoring, and predictor/diagnostic consistency require careful implementation.

related_work.title: Self-Attentive Sequential Recommendation
contributions: Provides the causal self-attention sequence encoder used as the starting model.
limitations: Implicit interaction associations do not directly establish practical compatibility or current purchase need.

related_work.title: TGCL4SR
contributions: Combines global temporal item-transition information with a local Transformer.
limitations: Does not establish gains for the proposed sparse residual on the pinned four-category benchmark.

related_work.title: LS4SRec
contributions: Uses weighted global item-transition information while separating long- and short-term interests.
limitations: Motivates temporal collaborative evidence without validating this implementation or its compatibility-related effects.

related_work.title: gSASRec
contributions: Investigates overconfidence under sampled BCE and proposes generalized BCE.
limitations: Loss calibration alone does not explicitly address stale interests and unsupported practical associations.

related_work.title: On Sampled Metrics for Item Recommendation
contributions: Shows that sampled ranking metrics can yield comparisons inconsistent with full-catalog evaluation.
limitations: Provides an evaluation caution rather than evidence that the proposed model improves recommendations.
